$chains: Fields, and which of them are load-bearing.
id           EIP-155. The only identifier that is not a matter of opinion.
key          our stable slug. Appears in URLs, so changing one is a breaking change.
aliases      what documents in the wild ACTUALLY write. Authors type a word, not an id, so
this decides whether a claim is readable at all. Must be lowercase and must not
collide with another chain: two chains claiming "base" makes a claim ambiguous,
and the conformance test refuses it.
rpcEnv       env var holding the endpoint. No endpoint means the chain reads as UNCOVERED,
and a claim naming it is `unknown`, never `false`. We did not look.
explorer     base URL for a human link. Cosmetic, and still required, because a hash nobody
can open is a worse citation than no hash.
erc8004      null when the registries are not deployed there. An object when they are, and
then the chain can carry agents, be indexed and be registered on.
The two dimensions are deliberately separate. A chain can be VERIFIABLE without hosting any
agents: Ethereum has no ERC-8004 registry here and we still read receipts on it, because an
agent registered on Monad may well be paid on Ethereum. That separation is the whole point of
